title: Milwaukee Officer Shoots Fleeing Driver While Clinging to Side of Tow Truck
description:
* (Disclaimer: The content in this video is intended for educational and informational purposes only)
Milwaukee, Wisconsin — On Thursday, March 12, 2026, at approximately 10:00 a.m., Milwaukee Police Department officers along with a Department of Corrections Agent responded to the 1900 block of South 12th Street to check for a wanted suspect with a parole violation. Upon arrival, an officer in full uniform encountered the suspect, later identified as 35-year-old Jonathan Otto, who was inside a full-sized flatbed tow truck with a passenger in the truck. The officer approached Otto and ordered that he exit the truck. Otto refused and the officer attempted to remove him from the truck at which time Otto immediately started the vehicle and suddenly drove off at a high rate of speed while the officer was clinging to Otto and the driver’s side window. Otto drove the truck for several blocks as the officer clung to the side of the truck. The officer gave several commands to Otto to stop the truck, even informing Otto that if he did not stop, he would shoot. Otto continued to refuse these commands multiple times. At this time, the officer discharged his firearm subsequently striking Otto, and finally stopping the truck. Otto, sustained fatal injuries. The passenger was not physically injured by the gunfire but was transported for medical treatment out of an abundance of caution. The officer that discharged his firearm is a 46-year-old male with over 21 years of service. He was transported to a hospital for treatment of non-fatal injuries. He was placed on administrative duty as is routine in officer involved shootings.
